title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 7: not elect as man/sinner; gratis dilecti; Aquinas dilectio/electio
pass_a_gloss: But as for what pertains to the latter part of the confirmation, where Gregory gathers: If men are not elected to glory inasmuch as they are foreseen well-working, then they are elected inasmuch as they are foreknown as men, or inasmuch as sinners; which since it belongs to all, election also would belong to all; this argumentation also is frivolous. For since the Philosophers rightly establish, What belongs to a thing inasmuch as such, belongs to every such, it is certain that God's election does not fall upon a human being inasmuch as a human being, nor upon a sinner inasmuch as a sinner, because from the event it is clear that it does not happen to all human beings, nor to all sinners, that they be elected. We therefore deny that distinction, Either God elects men inasmuch as they are foreseen about to cooperate with his grace, or inasmuch as they are foreknown as men or sinners, and we say that God elects men inasmuch as they were freely loved by him before others. If anyone further asks, Why these freely loved before others? the question is ridiculous: for the first cause of the divine will in the diffusion of its goods is the will itself; whose further cause is not to be sought. Not badly Aquinas; Part 1 q. 23 art. 4. Predestination of some unto eternal salvation presupposes according to reason that God wills their salvation. To which belong Election and Love: Love indeed, inasmuch as he wills them this good of eternal salvation; but Election, inasmuch as he wills them this good before others. And this will of God by which he wills a good to someone by loving is the cause that that good is had from him before others. And so it is clear that Love is presupposed to Election, and Election to predestination. Thus far he.
pass_b_english: As for Gregory's second support — if people are not elected to glory as foreseen working well, then they are elected as foreknown humans or as sinners, and since that belongs to all, election would belong to all — that too is frivolous. Philosophers rightly hold that what belongs to a thing as such belongs to every such; yet God's election does not fall on a person as human, nor on a sinner as sinner, because the event shows not all humans and not all sinners are elected. So we deny the fork Either God elects as foreseen cooperators with his grace, or as foreknown humans/sinners — and say he elects people as freely loved by him ahead of others. Why these freely loved ahead of others? A ridiculous question: the first cause of the divine will in pouring out its goods is the will itself; no further cause is to be hunted. Aquinas is not wrong (ST I q.23 a.4): predestination of some to eternal salvation presupposes that God wills their salvation. To that belong Love and Election: Love, inasmuch as he wills them this good of eternal salvation; Election, inasmuch as he wills them that good ahead of others. And that willing-by-loving is why they have the good from him ahead of others. So Love is presupposed to Election, and Election to predestination. So far Aquinas.
source_text: Quod autem attinet ad posteriorem partem confirmationis, ubi colligit Gregorius, Si homines non eligantur ad gloriam quatenus praevisi sunt bene operantes, tum electi sunt quatenus praesciuntur homines, vel quatenus peccatores; quod cum omnibus convenit, electio etiam omnibus conveniret; haec etiam argumentatio frivola est. Nam cum recte Philosophi statuunt, Quod convenit rei quatenus tali, convenit omni tali, certum est electionem Dei non cadere in hominem quatenus hominem, neque in peccatorem quatenus peccatorem, quia ex eventu liquet, non omnibus hominibus, neque omnibus peccatoribus contingere ut eligantur. Negamus ergo illam distinctionem, Aut Deus eligit homines quatenus praevidentur cooperaturi gratiae suae, aut quatenus praesciuntur ut homines vel peccatores, et dicimus Deum eligere homines quatenus sibi prae aliis fuerunt gratis dilecti. Siquis porro quaerat, Cur hi prae aliis gratis dilecti? ridicula quaestio est: nam prima causa voluntatis Divinae in diffusione suorum bonorum, est ipsa voluntas; cujus ulterior causa non est indaganda. Non male Aquinas; Part. 1. qu. 23. art. 4. Praedestinatio aliquorum in salutem aeternam praesupponit secundum rationem quod Deus velit eorum salutem. Ad quod pertinet Electio et Dilectio: Dilectio quidem, in quantum vult eis hoc bonum salutis aeternae; Electio autem, in quantum hoc bonum eis vult prae aliis. Et haec voluntas Dei qua vult bonum alicui diligendo, est causa quod illud bonum ab eo prae aliis habeatur. Et sic patet, quod Dilectio praesupponitur Electioni, et Electio praedestinationi. Hactenus ille.
